transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, what brings me in is... I feel like I’ve got a motor humming right under my skin. It happens whenever I’m supposed to just sit still. Like, if I'm in a staff meeting at work, or sitting through church event briefings, I just... I can't stay put. I always end up shifting around, standing up, or just finding some excuse to go move around. It's really been bothering me.
Do you often feel restless or have trouble staying still even when you're not in meetings or church events—like when you're at home relaxing or trying to focus on something quiet?

Yeah, it happens then too. Even when I’m just trying to relax on my own time. Like, if I'm out fishing with my wife, or we're sitting through a game of bingo... I always catch myself tapping, or I end up talking way too loud. I'll just keep messing with my tackle box, or fidgeting with the little pencil at bingo. It just... it gets really hard for me to just be quiet and actually enjoy the downtime.
Looking back, did you experience similar restlessness or trouble staying still when you were a child, like in school or during family gatherings?

Yeah, I did. I remember getting in trouble a lot back in grade school for popping out of my seat all the time. I was always talking over the teacher, or I'd just rush ahead and start doing things before they even finished giving the directions. My mother used to say I acted like I was wound too tight, even back then. So, yeah, it's been going on a long time.
